item.title: A Deadly Obsession: The Murder Trial of Dr. Kosowski | Case by Case | "48 Hours" Podcast
item.description: A missing lawyer, a plastic surgeon representing himself at trial, and a case filled with chilling details, including a murder bag and a paralyzing agent. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty and "48 Hours" consultant Herman Weisberg unpack the murder trial of Dr. Tomasz Kosowski and the evidence that led to his conviction for the murder of attorney Steven Cozzi.

item.title: Jane Doe's attorney says "she was incapable of consent," alleges cover-up
item.description: Jane Doe's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, tells CBS News the investigation into her alleged rape at a Cornell fraternity was a failure and university police "were in over their heads."

item.title: CBS News poll finds voters split on state v. national focus in Maine Senate race
item.description: Troy Jackson is boosted by those looking for change, while Collins peels off some Trump disapprovers.

item.title: Trump says Europe will release "massive amount" of diesel oil from stockpiles
item.description: A joint statement from G7 world leaders confirmed there will be a "coordinated release" of 100 million barrels, to begin "immediately."

item.title: Environmental groups sue Trump administration over vehicle MPG rollback
item.description: Reducing fuel-efficiency standards will raise prices at the pump and produce more harmful emissions, according to environmentalists.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Oct. 4, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 4)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Book excerpt: "Narratives" by Nancy Colier
item.description: In her latest book, the psychotherapist writes about how the stories we tell ourselves about ourselves can hold us back from living a more truthful and connected life.

item.title: Christa Pike unconscious, on ventilator after botched execution, lawyers say
item.description: Christa Pike "remains critically ill" and is receiving medical care after a botched execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said.

item.title: In Cornell investigation, Gov. Hochul says AG James will find out "how was this woman denied justice"
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul has tapped New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the Cornell University alleged rape case.

item.title: Trump vows Iran war to end "very quickly" as more troops head to Mideast
item.description: Some 9,000 more U.S. forces are headed for the Middle East as President Trump vows the war will end "right after the election," if not sooner.

item.title: American Airlines will let travelers mix cash and miles to pay for flights
item.description: As holiday airfares spike, American Airlines plans to let travelers pay for flights with a mix of cash and loyalty points.

item.title: David Rivera sentenced to 10 years in Venezuela lobbying case
item.description: Former U.S. Rep. David Rivera was convicted on federal charges stemming from a secret lobbying campaign tied to the Venezuelan government.

item.title: Supreme Court Justice Alito on deciding when to retire
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito said he decided to remain on the Supreme Court because he believed he could "still make a valuable contribution." The 76-year-old justice said he expects to reconsider his decision each year. He sat down with CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford in an interview airing Monday.

item.title: Alito recalls being more recognized after his Supreme Court confirmation hearings
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito said he doesn't get recognized in public often. "I was recognized much more frequently after my confirmation hearings," he recalled. CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford sat down with Alito on the bleachers of the New Jersey baseball field where he played as a boy for an interview airing Monday.

item.title: Alito says criticism of Supreme Court from political leaders can be "quite damaging"
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito told CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford that increasingly harsh criticism of the court from political leaders can be "quite damaging" to the institution. In an interview airing Monday, Alito said criticism from former President Joe Biden and President Trump has been "very harsh."

item.title: Alito says he lost friends over Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito told CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford that he lost friends over his decision in the 2022 Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization case, which overturned Roe v. Wade. "It's part of the job that you're going to displease people by making decisions on controversial matters," Alito said in an interview airing Monday.

item.title: European leaders agree to release diesel reserve, Trump says amid midterms push
item.description: President Trump is campaigning in typically red states ahead of Election Day. He says some European leaders have agreed to release part of their fuel reserves to alleviate high prices. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard's partner, Ken Urker, dies at 34
item.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard and Ken Urker connected while she was in prison for the 2015 murder of her mother, Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard.

item.title: Kennedy Center Honors to take place at a different venue
item.description: Efforts to put President Trump's name on the Kennedy Center continue, despite a court's order blocking such a change.

item.title: New body cam footage of Luigi Mangione arrest inside Pennsylvania McDonald's
item.description: New body cam footage has been released of the moment Luigi Mangione was arrested inside a Pennsylvania McDonald's. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: How some AI models are more vulnerable to manipulation
item.description: China has embraced open-weight models, a development that researchers say is closing the AI capability gap between the country and the U.S.

item.title: Amazon vows to invest $1 billion in areas where it builds data centers
item.description: Amazon said it will invest $1 billion over five years to support job education, energy affordability and other priorities in communities where its data centers are located.

item.title: The AI revolution is likely to drive up your electricity bill. Here's why.
item.description: Utilities are racing to build data centers to meet surging demand for AI and other tech services. Ratepayers will pick up the tab, experts say.

item.title: Cornell student body feels "let down" by university, student leader says
item.description: Adriana Vink said dozens of students attended a town hall to discuss the administration's response to campus sexual violence.

item.title: Amazon Prime customers could get $200 refunds in expanded FTC deal
item.description: Some Amazon customers could receive refunds of up to $200. Here's who is eligible for a payment and when consumers will get the money.

item.title: Hochul on "troubling questions" in the Cornell rape case, says it exposes gap in state consent law
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul addressed the Cornell University gang rape allegations and said state Attorney General Letitia James will investigate the claims. Hochul also said the case is exposing a gap in state laws surrounding intoxication and consent. CBS News' Tom Hanson has more.

item.title: Senate approves sweeping bill to regulate college sports
item.description: The Senate on Thursday approved a sweeping college sports bill to establish a federal framework for college athletics aimed at protecting student athletes — despite some pushback from some Democrats who argue that it could do the opposite.

item.title: 9/13: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," with the midterm elections less than two months away, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto returns with the Battleground Tracker. Plus, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Utah Gov. Spencer Cox join.

item.title: 9/6: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," with midterm elections less than two months away, Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson joins as well as Reps. Jason Crow and Lisa McClain. Plus, Sunoco chairman and Republican midterm convention chair Ray Washburne joins.
